title: Creating and reading arrays
learningObjectives: Explain creating and reading arrays and process JavaScript collections correctly.

understand.concept: An array is an ordered collection of values. Arrays are created with [] or the Array constructor and accessed using zero-based indexes. The length property reports the number of elements. Arrays can contain values of different types, though consistent element types often improve clarity.
understand.whyItMatters: Arrays are useful for ordered lists such as lessons, topics, and learner results. Check indexes and length because an invalid index returns undefined.
understand.analogy: An array is like a numbered row of storage slots; the first slot is index zero.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript array and object methods have defined mutation, iteration, and reference semantics.

explain.narrative: The first item is HTML, the third is JavaScript, and the array length is three.

examples.explanation: The first item is HTML, the third is JavaScript, and the array length is three.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the array or object values described.

practise.guidedTask: Create an array of five course topics. Read the first and last values and display the length.
practise.independentTask: Build a small collection-processing example using arrays and objects. Test empty collections, missing values, and mutation behaviour.
hints: Check whether a method mutates or returns a new value.
Use clear object property names and deliberate copying.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Creating and reading arrays</title></head><body>
<script>const topics=['HTML','CSS','JavaScript'];console.log(topics[0],topics[2],topics.length);</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: What is the index of the first array element?
What should you check when using an array method?
options: Whether it mutates the source or returns a new value
Whether the array contains strings only
questions.answer: Whether it mutates the source or returns a new value
questions.explanation: Mutation behaviour matters when arrays are shared across application code.
